newsitem.title: NIGERIA: SOCCER-NIGERIA CALL UP LEYTON PLAYER FOR WORLD CUP QUALIFIER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NIGERIA CALL UP LEYTON PLAYER FOR WORLD CUP QUALIFIER.

text.p: Olympic champions Nigeria on Wednesday enlarged its squad by inviting English divison three club Leyton Orient midfielder Samuel Ayorinde and five others for Saturday's World Cup qualifying game against Burkina Faso.
"We decided to increase the number invited for the game to give everyone a chance to prove his worth," coach Amodu Shaibu said.
Shaibu last month named two separate squads for the World Cup qualifier and a friendly against Turkey in Istanbul played last week when Nigeria lost 3-2.
"Some people we wanted to evaluate with the Turkey friendly did not turn up because of club commitments. It's only fair to use the Burkina Faso game to assess them," he said.

Olympic team keeper Joseph Dosu of Italian club Reggiana, Monaco striker Victor Ikpeba, defenders Uche Okafor and Ben Iroha, who are playing in the U.S. Major League Soccer and former national captain Austin Eguavoen were the other newly-invited players.
A total of 24 players will now struggle for the 16 available places on Saturday, Shaibu said.
"I know this will give me selection worries of getting the best for the game," he said, acknowledging: "And there is the added pressure of the need for us to win at home."
Goalkeepers: Willy Okpara (Orlando Pirates, South Africa), Ike Shorounmu (FC Zurich, Switzerland), Joseph Dosu (Reggiana, Italy)

Defenders: Celestine Babayaro (Anderlecht, Belgium), Austin Eguavoen (Unattached), Mobi Oparaku (Turnhout, Belgium), Taribo West (Auxerre, France), Uche Okechukwu (Fenerbache, Turkey), Uche Okafor (Kansas City, United States), Ben Iroha (San Jose Clash, United States), Chidi Nwanu (Anderlecht, Belgium)

Midfielders: Austin Jay-Jay Okocha (Fenerbahce, Turkey), Garba Lawal (FC Utrecht, Netherlands), Mutiu Adepoju (Racing Santander, Spain), Samuel Ayorinde (Leyton Orient, England), Sunday Oliseh (Colgne, Germany), Godwin Opara (Strasbourg, France)

Strikers: Rashidi Yekini (Sporting Gijon, Spain), Finidi George (Real Betis, Spain), Victor Ikpeba (Monaco, France), Jonathan Akpoborie (Hansa Rostock, Germany), Daniel Amokachi (Besiktas, Turkey), Emmanuel Amunike (Sporting Lisbon, Portugal), Tijjani Babangida (Ajax Amsterdam, Netherlands).
